subject: MSA/Order Form - negotiation on fraud / willful misconduct / gross negligence carve-outs
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmesoft.com
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA / Order Form - carve-out for gross negligence & proof burden

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. Our GC asked me to follow up on the MSA/Order Form redlines you received. To avoid scope creep on other items, the main open question for Acme is the liability carve-outs and how you want to treat fraud, willful misconduct and gross negligence. Our starting point: unlimited liability for proven fraud or intentional misconduct; a narrower exclusion for gross negligence only where there is clear and convincing evidence and a materiality threshold.

We have a couple of practical asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept unlimited liability for fraud proven by final adjudication or criminal conviction.
- If Redwood insists on a cap or threshold for willful misconduct/gross negligence, what standard of proof will you require and what objective thresholds (e.g., monetary, demonstrable production impact) are you proposing?
- We also need to understand evidence/backing: will Redwood provide audit logs and internal investigation reports when requested?

Can you share suggested redline language that aligns with your risk tolerances? I can then run it by our GC (cc'd). I attached our marked-up MSA for context.

Thanks,

Sara Nguyen
Head of Procurement, Acme Soft
Acme Soft
(attachment: Acme_MSARedlines_red.pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - carve-out for gross negligence & proof burden

Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. I've run this past our legal and commercial teams; sending a short summary and an initial compromise proposal (attached). Key points from Redwood's side:

- Fraud: Redwood can accept an unlimited-liability carve-out for fraud proven by final adjudication or criminal conviction. That avoids open-ended discovery risk while giving Acme the protection you need.

- Willful misconduct / intentional fraud: we are prepared to treat "knowing and intentional" misconduct as outside the cap, again subject to final adjudication.

- Gross negligence: we are uncomfortable with an unlimited carve-out. Proposed approach: limit the carve-out to direct damages above a monetary threshold (we propose $500,000) and require a showing of material breach tied to demonstrable customer impact (suggested definition below).

- Burden/standard of proof: for fraud (criminal/final order) — final adjudication standard. For allegations of gross negligence, we propose preponderance of evidence plus written notice and a 30-day remediation window; if the conduct is egregious and proven by clear and convincing evidence, the cap would not apply.

- Evidence access: Redwood will provide applicable audit logs and incident timelines on a reasonable basis and subject to a protective order for sensitive internal details. We can't commit to sharing privileged investigation memos.

Proposed sample language (in the attached redline):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, liability shall not be limited or excluded for (a) proven fraud or criminal misconduct as finally adjudicated in a court of competent jurisdiction, or (b) willful and knowing misconduct as established by such final adjudication. For gross negligence, Customer's recoverable damages shall be limited to direct damages in excess of $500,000, provided that (i) Customer provides prompt written notice, (ii) Redwood is given a 30-day opportunity to cure, and (iii) Customer demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that the conduct caused material impairment to Customer's production systems (material impairment defined as unavailability or corruption affecting primary production systems for at least 72 consecutive hours)."

I've attached redlines (redlines_MSA_v3.docx) with the precise wording. Happy to hop on a short call with GC to work through exact phrasing.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redlines_MSA_v3.docx)

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-28T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - carve-out for gross negligence & proof burden

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick response and the draft language. A few clarifications from our GC:

- Acme's position remains that willful misconduct and fraud should be unlimited and not dependent on a money threshold. We want to avoid situations where a deliberate, damaging act is effectively covered by a cap because the loss calculation is messy.

- For gross negligence, Acme would prefer that it be carved out in cases of reckless conduct that led to significant customer harm; however, we accept a formulation tied to final adjudication or criminal conviction as one path. We do not want the only path to be a court order — we asked whether an independent expert determination (agreed by both parties) could also establish the standard.

- Regarding evidence, Acme needs reasonable access to logs and incident timelines; if Redwood requires a protective order for investigation memos, that's acceptable, but we need a commitment to cooperate.

I've attached our redlines for your team to review (Acme_MSARedlines_red.pdf). Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to try to close this? Our GC is available at 10:30 PT.

Regards,

Sara
(attachment: Acme_MSARedlines_red.pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-29T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - negotiation summary and next steps

Sara —

Thanks — summarizing our positions and a proposed path forward so the call is efficient:

1) Fraud / knowing and intentional misconduct
- Redwood: unlimited liability if proven by final adjudication or criminal conviction.
- Acme: prefers unlimited without requiring court; suggests independent expert as alternative.
- Proposed compromise: unlimited for (i) final adjudication or criminal conviction, or (ii) a written determination by an independent expert jointly appointed by the parties (with rules for selecting the expert and scope limited to whether the conduct meets the agreed definition of fraud or willful misconduct).

2) Gross negligence / reckless conduct
- Redwood: keep within cap; suggest $500k monetary threshold and cure period. Materiality tied to production impact (72 consecutive hours).
- Acme: wants carve-out where reckless conduct caused significant harm; open to independent expert or adjudication paths.
- Proposed compromise: gross negligence that (a) is proven by final adjudication, criminal conviction, or independent expert determination, or (b) where Redwood's reckless act caused direct damages exceeding $500,000 and Customer demonstrates material impairment (72h) — in these limited cases the cap does not apply.

3) Evidence and cooperation
- Redwood will provide relevant audit logs and incident timelines; privileged investigation materials will be subject to protective order.
- Both parties to agree SLA for producing logs (target: 10 business days from written request unless emergency).

Next steps
- If Acme agrees in principle to the independent expert path and the $500k threshold for gross negligence carve-out, our legal team will produce a redline with the exact expert selection mechanics and the notification/cure language.
- Let's take the 30-minute call tomorrow (10:30 PT). I'll have lauren and marissa join. If you confirm, I'll send a calendar invite and a draft redline by end of day.
